headline: Accounting & Financial Services · Spanish · Master
threshold: Use Spanish to complete the master accounting & financial services conversations and explain the next step.

lessons.title: Resolve an unexplained reconciliation difference
lessons.objective: Revise a reconciliation after a missing transaction appears, document the evidence in Spanish and explain the change to a colleague without overstating certainty.
lessons.focus: Present perfect for what has changed so far (ha aparecido, hemos revisado), subjunctive after no creo que for uncertainty, and the impersonal se for documentation.

words.note: Matching two records and explaining every difference.
An item present in one record but not matched to the other.
The bank's summary for a period.
The evidence that proves a transaction.
A difference left after known items are matched.
A change made to correct the record.
To record the evidence and the reason for a change.
The review of records before the period closes.
A fee or debit taken by the bank.
A written explanation of the matching steps and open items.
The date a payment counts as settled.
The system that records and reports financial activity.

words.es: Ha aparecido una partida nueva en el extracto.
words.en: A new item has appeared on the statement.

words.es: No creo que sea un error del banco.
words.en: I do not think it is an error by the bank.

words.es: Revisemos la prueba antes de cambiar el saldo.
words.en: Let's review the evidence before changing the balance.

words.es: Documentamos el ajuste en la nota de conciliación.
words.en: We document the adjustment in the reconciliation note.

words.es: La diferencia residual queda pendiente hasta el justificante.
words.en: The residual difference stays open until the supporting document arrives.

words.es: ¿Qué cambio tiene que documentar para el cierre?
words.en: What change do you have to document for the close?

lessons.speaking: Explain to a colleague that a transaction you first treated as reconciled has now appeared. Describe the evidence, revise the reconciliation, state what remains uncertain and agree the documentation step before the close.
lessons.partnerRole: Colleague who approved the first reconciliation and now asks why it changed.
lessons.openingLine: Creía que la conciliación estaba lista, pero el banco mandó otra partida. ¿Qué pasó?

grammar.focus: Use the present perfect for a change that has happened by now: ha aparecido una partida nueva. No creo que plus the subjunctive states uncertainty: no creo que sea un error del banco. Passive se (se documenta el cambio; se documentan los cambios) keeps the focus on the record rather than the person who made it.

examples.es: Ha aparecido una partida nueva que no estaba en el primer extracto.
examples.en: A new item has appeared that was not on the first statement.

examples.es: No creo que el error sea del banco; primero necesitamos la prueba.
examples.en: I do not think the error is the bank's; first we need the evidence.

lessons.title: Handle conflicting client records
lessons.objective: Handle two conflicting client records in Spanish by identifying the conflict, requesting the source needed to resolve it and agreeing a neutral next step.
lessons.focus: Subjunctive after es necesario que and para que, with comparative and contrast vocabulary for two documents.

words.note: A document that disagrees with another on the same item.
The original record used to check a figure.
The money figure on a document.
A difference between two figures that should match.
The person or business whose records are reviewed.
The first invoice issued, before any correction.
A document that reduces an amount previously invoiced.
The bank or account summary.
The check of which record is the reliable one.
A payment that settles only part of an amount due.
The time allowed for the source to be provided.
Written proof that a figure has been checked.
The choice made once the records are compared.
The person responsible for keeping a record accurate.

words.es: Hay dos documentos con cifras distintas para el mismo pago.
words.en: There are two documents with different figures for the same payment.

words.es: Es necesario que revisemos la fuente original.
words.en: It is necessary that we review the original source.

words.es: Pido la factura original para confirmar el importe.
words.en: I request the original invoice to confirm the amount.

words.es: ¿Qué documento refleja la nota de crédito?
words.en: Which document reflects the credit note?
words.note: Qué before a noun is standard everywhere; cuál before a noun is heard in parts of Latin America.

words.es: Esperamos la confirmación antes de decidir.
words.en: We wait for the confirmation before deciding.

words.es: No cambiamos el registro hasta tener la prueba.
words.en: We do not change the record until we have the evidence.

lessons.speaking: Discuss two documents that give different amounts for the same payment. State the conflict neutrally, request the source document with a clear deadline, and agree who will check which record. Close by repeating the agreed step.
lessons.partnerRole: Client who believes one of two documents is wrong and wants to know which one to trust.
lessons.openingLine: Tengo dos documentos con cifras distintas para el mismo pago. ¿Cuál es el correcto?

grammar.focus: Es necesario que plus the subjunctive states what must happen: es necesario que revisemos la fuente. Para que plus the subjunctive gives a purpose when the subject changes: la pido para que confirmemos el importe. Mientras tanto marks the waiting period.

examples.es: Es necesario que revisemos la fuente original antes de decidir.
examples.en: It is necessary that we review the original source before deciding.

examples.es: Pido la factura del proveedor para que confirmemos el importe.
examples.en: I request the supplier invoice so that we can confirm the amount.

lessons.title: Discuss a late or incomplete submission
lessons.objective: Discuss a late and incomplete submission in Spanish by agreeing responsibilities, naming the missing records and communicating the uncertainty that remains.
lessons.focus: Future for a planned action (presentaremos), temo que plus the subjunctive for a deadline concern, and the conditional for a fallback (presentaríamos).

words.note: Formal sending of a return or document.
The last date for a submission.
Records that do not yet cover the whole task.
A version sent before all records arrive, marked as subject to change.
The person who owns a task.
The part of the outcome that is not yet known.
A proof of payment.
Additional time granted for a submission, if the other party agrees.
A plan used if the first one cannot be met.
A message explaining status and next steps.
A record of what was sent and when.
The last date for an action.
The current state of a client file.

words.es: Faltan dos recibos y el plazo es el viernes.
words.en: Two receipts are missing and the deadline is Friday.

words.es: Temo que no lleguemos a tiempo.
words.en: I am afraid we will not make it on time.

words.es: Presentaremos los estados financieros el jueves si llegan los recibos.
words.en: We will submit the financial statements on Thursday if the receipts arrive.

words.es: Presentaríamos una versión provisional como plan alternativo.
words.en: We would submit a provisional version as the fallback plan.

words.es: Le comunico la incertidumbre que queda.
words.en: Let me tell you the uncertainty that remains.

words.es: ¿Quién es el responsable de cada documento?
words.en: Who is responsible for each document?

lessons.speaking: Speak with a client two days before the date the bank requires the annual financial statements under a loan agreement, with two receipts still missing. Name the missing items and who owns each one, state the remaining uncertainty without overstating it, and agree a fallback plan with a date.
lessons.partnerRole: Client who thinks the statements for the bank will be complete on time and does not want to hear about gaps.
lessons.openingLine: Faltan dos recibos y el plazo es el viernes. ¿Vamos a llegar a tiempo?

grammar.focus: Temo que plus the subjunctive expresses a concern: temo que no lleguemos a tiempo. The future plans the action: presentaremos los estados el jueves. A hypothetical fallback uses si plus the imperfect subjunctive with the conditional: si no llegaran, presentaríamos una versión provisional.

examples.es: Temo que no lleguemos a tiempo si faltan los recibos del proveedor.
examples.en: I am afraid we will not make it on time if the supplier receipts are missing.

examples.es: Si no llegaran los recibos, presentaríamos una versión provisional.
examples.en: If the receipts did not arrive, we would submit a provisional version.

lessons.title: Explain a material correction to a client
lessons.objective: Explain a material correction to a client in Spanish by separating a confirmed error from effects that are still under review, using the passive se and the subjunctive for doubt.
lessons.focus: Confirmed error with se and the preterite (se detectó), effects under review with estar plus the gerund, and doubt with es posible que plus the subjunctive; no sé si takes the indicative.

words.note: An error large enough to change a decision. Error material in Spanish usually means a clerical slip, not a material error.
The revised version that replaces an earlier report.
The consequence of a correction on other figures.
Established by evidence.
Still being checked.
A written notice of a correction.
The right figure after review.
The date when the revised report will arrive.
A choice the client made using the earlier report.
A written note that explains the change.
To put a revised item in place of the earlier one.
The effect of a change on a result.

words.es: Se detectó un error de importe en el informe de enero.
words.en: An amount error was detected in the January report.

words.es: Estamos revisando si el efecto será mayor.
words.en: We are reviewing whether the effect will be larger.

words.es: No debe tomar una decisión con la cifra anterior.
words.en: You should not make a decision with the earlier figure.

words.es: Le enviamos el informe corregido el jueves.
words.en: We will send you the corrected report on Thursday.

words.es: El error está confirmado; el impacto todavía no.
words.en: The error is confirmed; the impact is not yet.

words.es: Le pido disculpas por la confusión que causó.
words.en: I apologize for the confusion it caused.

lessons.speaking: Explain to a client that an earlier report needs a revision. State what is confirmed, what is still being reviewed, and what the client should not rely on yet. Close by agreeing the date of the revised report.
lessons.partnerRole: Client who relied on the earlier report to make a decision and is upset.
lessons.openingLine: Me dijeron que el informe estaba bien y ahora me llaman con otra cifra. ¿Qué pasó?

grammar.focus: Se with the preterite (se detectó un error) reports a confirmed error without naming a person. Estar plus the gerund (estamos revisando) marks work in progress. Es posible que takes the subjunctive: es posible que el efecto sea mayor; no sé si takes the indicative: no sé si será mayor.

examples.es: Se detectó un error de importe en el informe de enero.
examples.en: An amount error was detected in the January report.

examples.es: Es posible que el efecto en el impuesto sea mayor.
examples.en: The effect on the tax may be larger.

lessons.title: Respond to an anxious tax client
lessons.objective: Respond to an anxious tax client in Spain by reading a proposed assessment from the Agencia Tributaria together, separating it from a final bill and clarifying the reply it requests.
lessons.focus: Imperatives for joint review (leamos, vea, revisemos), and the relative clause que requests with the indicative for a fact.

words.note: A written communication from a tax authority.
The tax agency's final assessment of the amount due, which states how and when to pay.
In Spain, a proposed tax assessment that allows a reply, called alegaciones, before the final assessment.
The time allowed to reply.
The government body that issues notices.
The amount the tax agency proposes; it is not yet final.
A payment demanded at once.
Records that justify the figures.
A professional who reviews notices.
A written explanation requested by the authority.
In tax, cuota is the tax amount itself (cuota tributaria). On a loan, cuota is an installment.
A charge for a violation, where it applies.

words.es: ¿Qué tipo de aviso es este documento?
words.en: What type of notice is this document?

words.es: Leamos el aviso juntos antes de pagar.
words.en: Let's read the notice together before paying.

words.es: El aviso permite responder con documentación de respaldo.
words.en: The notice allows a reply with supporting documentation.

words.es: Este aviso no es la liquidación final.
words.en: This notice is not the final bill.

words.es: ¿Cuál es el plazo de respuesta que indica?
words.en: What response deadline does it state?

words.es: Mantenga los documentos a mano hasta la respuesta.
words.en: Keep the documents to hand until the reply.

lessons.speaking: Read a tax notice with an anxious client. Confirm what the notice says it is, distinguish it from the final bill, name the action it requests and its deadline. Ask the client to repeat the action, then agree the next step.
lessons.partnerRole: Anxious client in Spain who believes a proposed assessment from the tax agency is a final bill and wants to pay immediately.
lessons.openingLine: Recibí una carta de la Agencia Tributaria y dice que debo pagar mucho. ¿Lo pago ya?

grammar.focus: Nosotros commands invite joint action: leamos el aviso juntos. Usted commands direct the client to a line: vea, mantenga. A relative clause with que plus the indicative states a fact about a known document: el aviso que recibió pide una respuesta.

examples.es: Leamos el aviso juntos antes de pagar cualquier cantidad.
examples.en: Let's read the notice together before paying any amount.

examples.es: El aviso que recibió pide una respuesta antes de la fecha límite.
examples.en: The notice you received asks for a reply before the deadline.

lessons.title: Compare planning alternatives
lessons.objective: Compare two fictional equipment-funding options in Spanish, stating assumptions, costs and tradeoffs without claiming one option is universally best.
lessons.focus: Conditional (sería, tendríamos) for hypothetical outcomes, si plus imperfect subjunctive for an unlikely condition, and comparisons with más ... que and menos ... que.

words.note: A contract to use an asset for a fixed period against regular payments.
Buying an asset with borrowed money. Spain usually says financiación; financiamiento is common in Latin America.
A condition the comparison depends on.
Costs paid at the start of the arrangement.
All payments added together over the term.
The value of the asset at the end of the arrangement.
A possible case the options are tested against.
The ability to change plans as conditions change.
Costs to keep the asset in working order.
The reduction in an asset's recorded value over time.
The percentage charged on borrowed money.
A possible loss or unfavorable outcome.
A structured look at two or more options.
The advice given after comparing options.

words.en: Leasing costs less at the start.

words.es: Si el volumen subiera, la compra tendría más sentido.
words.en: If the volume went up, buying would make more sense.

words.es: El supuesto principal es el volumen de entregas.
words.en: The main assumption is the volume of deliveries.

words.es: No existe una opción universalmente mejor.
words.en: There is no universally better option.

words.es: Revisemos ambos escenarios antes de decidir.
words.en: Let's review both scenarios before deciding.

lessons.speaking: Compare leasing and buying a delivery van for a fictional bakery. Name the assumption each option depends on, state two costs and one tradeoff for each, and say which factor would change the recommendation. Close by agreeing what data is needed before deciding.
lessons.partnerRole: Bakery owner who wants a clear comparison of two funding options before a bank meeting.
lessons.openingLine: Podemos comprar la furgoneta o arrendarla. ¿Qué nos conviene más?

grammar.focus: Conditional sería and tendríamos describe a hypothetical result: si el volumen subiera, la compra sería mejor. Si plus imperfect subjunctive describes an unlikely condition: si vendiéramos el doble, podríamos pagar más rápido. Compare options with más ... que and menos ... que, and state the assumption before the conclusion.

examples.es: Si el volumen de entregas subiera, la compra tendría más sentido.
examples.en: If the delivery volume went up, buying would make more sense.

examples.es: Arrendar cuesta menos al inicio, pero el pago total es más alto.
examples.en: Leasing costs less at the start, but the total payment is higher.

lessons.title: Discuss a tax estimate that changed
lessons.objective: Explain in Spanish how a new income item changed a self-employed client's tax estimate in Spain, state the changed assumption and name the next review step, with the preterite for the event and the present perfect for the update.
lessons.focus: Preterite for the event that changed the estimate (llegó, cambió) and the present perfect for work already updated (hemos actualizado), with the subjunctive after es posible que.

words.note: A provisional calculation of tax owed.
A newly received income item that affects the estimate.
The assumption that no longer holds.
In Spain, a quarterly IRPF advance many self-employed workers make. It counts toward the year's tax.
The amount on which tax is calculated.
A check of figures before they are final.
The settled figure after all adjustments.
A written agreement that creates the income.
A three-month period used for estimates.
A change made at the final calculation.
The action that comes after the update.
The arithmetic that produces the estimate.
A professional who reviews the estimate.

words.es: Llegó un pago grande en mayo.
words.en: A large payment arrived in May.

words.es: Hemos actualizado la estimación del trimestre.
words.en: We have updated the quarter's estimate.

words.es: Es posible que el monto final cambie.
words.en: It is possible that the final amount will change.

words.es: El supuesto cambiado es el ingreso del contrato nuevo.
words.en: The changed assumption is the income from the new contract.

words.es: ¿Cuál es el próximo paso de la revisión?
words.en: What is the next step of the review?

words.es: La regularización se hace en la declaración anual.
words.en: The adjustment is made in the annual return.

lessons.speaking: Walk a self-employed client through the revised estimate. Name the new income item and its date, state the assumption that changed, explain what the revision does and does not decide, and agree the next review step with a date.
lessons.partnerRole: Self-employed client in Spain who received a large payment from a new contract and wants to know whether the tax estimate changes.
lessons.openingLine: Me llegó un pago grande de un contrato nuevo. ¿Cambia mi estimación de impuestos?

grammar.focus: The preterite marks the event that changed the estimate: el pago llegó en mayo. The present perfect records the update so far: hemos actualizado la estimación. Es posible que plus the subjunctive names an uncertain consequence: es posible que el pago suba.

examples.es: Llegó un pago grande en mayo y cambió la estimación del trimestre.
examples.en: A large payment arrived in May and changed the quarter's estimate.

examples.es: Hemos actualizado la estimación, pero es posible que el monto final cambie.
examples.en: We have updated the estimate, but the final amount may change.

lessons.title: Resolve a payroll discrepancy
lessons.objective: Resolve a payroll discrepancy in Spanish by comparing an employee's hours with the time record, the approval and the payroll statement, using the conditional to propose a check.
lessons.focus: Conditional (revisaríamos, corregiríamos) for a proposed check, the imperfect for what a record showed, and passive se (se aprobó) to report an approval without naming a person.

words.note: The system or sheet that logs hours worked.
The time actually spent on the job.
The hours included in the payslip.
The manager's authorization of the hours.
The statement of pay and deductions.
Hours beyond the agreed schedule.
A difference between two records that should match.
A change that fixes a record.
The person who approves time records.
The time covered by the payslip.
A payment made to correct an underpayment.
The system of wages.
A request from an employee about pay.

words.es: Trabajé más horas de las que aparecen en el recibo.
words.en: I worked more hours than appear on the payslip.

words.es: Revisaríamos el registro de tiempo antes de corregir.
words.en: We would review the time record before correcting.

words.es: El supervisor aprobó 46 horas en el periodo.
words.en: The supervisor approved 46 hours in the period.

words.es: Se aprobó un registro distinto al del recibo.
words.en: A different record was approved from the one on the payslip.

words.es: La corrección aparecerá en el próximo recibo.
words.en: The correction will appear on the next payslip.

lessons.speaking: Speak with an employee who reports fewer paid hours than worked. Compare the time record with the approval and the payroll statement, identify the difference, propose the check and the correction. Agree the date when the employee will see the corrected payslip.
lessons.partnerRole: Employee who worked extra hours in the last two weeks and sees fewer paid hours on the payslip.
lessons.openingLine: Trabajé más horas de las que aparecen en el recibo de nómina. ¿Qué pasó?

grammar.focus: The conditional proposes a check politely: primero revisaríamos el registro. The imperfect describes what a record showed: el registro indicaba 46 horas. Passive se (se aprobó) reports what was approved without naming who approved it.

examples.es: Revisaríamos el registro de tiempo antes de corregir el recibo.
examples.en: We would review the time record before correcting the payslip.

examples.es: El registro indicaba 46 horas, pero el recibo solo mostraba 40.
examples.en: The record showed 46 hours, but the payslip only showed 40.

lessons.title: Handle a disputed vendor payment
lessons.objective: Handle a disputed vendor payment in Spanish by verifying references, asking for the bank trace and agreeing a correction process without assigning blame.
lessons.focus: Present perfect for what has been verified (hemos verificado), the subjunctive after es posible que and no creo que, and the impersonal se for the trace process.

words.note: A payment the vendor says it did not receive.
The code that links a payment to an invoice.
A search through the bank for a payment's route.
Proof that a transfer was sent.
A business that supplies goods or services.
The money figure of the payment.
The date a payment is settled.
A delay placed on a transfer by the bank.
A fix made after the trace.
The time the bank needs to complete a trace.
The agreed steps for resolving the dispute.
The bill the payment settles.
The matching of records.

words.es: Hemos verificado la referencia y el importe.
words.en: We have verified the reference and the amount.

words.es: Es posible que el banco haya retenido la transferencia.
words.en: It is possible that the bank has held the transfer.

words.es: Se pide el rastreo bancario al banco.
words.en: The bank trace is requested from the bank.

words.es: No creo que les hayan avisado del cambio.
words.en: I do not think anyone told you about the change.

words.es: ¿Cuál es el plazo de rastreo del banco?
words.en: What is the bank's trace period?

words.es: Acordamos el procedimiento para la corrección.
words.en: We agree on the procedure for the correction.

lessons.speaking: Respond to a vendor who says the payment never arrived. Verify the reference and amount, ask for the bank trace, and agree a neutral correction process with a date. Close by stating what remains unverified.
lessons.partnerRole: Vendor who says a payment never arrived and wants it resent immediately.
lessons.openingLine: Hace dos semanas nos pagaron y no ha llegado nada. ¿Qué pasó con la transferencia?

grammar.focus: Present perfect describes checks completed: hemos verificado la referencia. Es posible que plus subjunctive names an unknown cause: es posible que la referencia esté mal escrita. Passive se describes a process without naming the person: se pide el rastreo al banco; se piden los rastreos.

examples.es: Hemos verificado la referencia y el importe, pero el pago no aparece todavía.
examples.en: We have verified the reference and the amount, but the payment does not appear yet.

examples.es: Es posible que el banco haya retenido la transferencia por una verificación.
examples.en: It is possible that the bank held the transfer for a check.

lessons.title: Explain a cash shortage despite profit
lessons.objective: Explain a cash shortage to a business owner in Spanish when profit exists, tracing timing differences and restricted cash, without treating profit as cash.
lessons.focus: Gerund for a process (cobrando, pagando), the pronoun se in the phrase se queda sin efectivo, and the contrast between aunque and sin embargo.

words.note: Cash that cannot be used freely, such as a reserve or deposit.
The recorded result after expenses.
A gap between when revenue is recorded and when cash moves.
Amounts clients owe the business.
Amounts the business owes suppliers.
A payment set for a fixed date.
Cash held back for emergencies.
Cash in and out over a period.
Money needed for daily operations.
An agreed limit the business can borrow against.
Cash held as security, for example in an account the lender requires. It is not available for daily payments.
Cash kept in the business.
The schedule of payments against cash in.

words.es: La utilidad es positiva; sin embargo, el efectivo está comprometido.
words.en: Profit is positive; however, the cash is committed.

words.es: Estamos cobrando las ventas a treinta días.
words.en: We are collecting sales on thirty-day terms.

words.es: El depósito de garantía no está disponible.
words.en: The security deposit is not available.
Which scheduled payments fall due this week?

words.es: Revisemos la planificación de pagos juntos.
words.en: Let's review the payment planning together.

words.es: Se queda sin efectivo si pagamos antes de cobrar.
words.en: It runs out of cash if we pay before collecting.

lessons.speaking: Explain to an owner why profit is positive but a payment cannot be funded. Trace the timing, name one restricted or reserved amount, and state what the owner can do this week. Ask the owner to repeat the cash position before agreeing the action.
lessons.partnerRole: Owner who sees profit on the report but cannot fund a supplier payment due this week.
lessons.openingLine: Tenemos utilidad, pero no puedo pagar al proveedor esta semana. ¿Dónde está el dinero?

grammar.focus: The gerund shows an ongoing process: estamos cobrando las ventas a treinta días. Se queda sin efectivo describes a state arising from timing. Sin embargo introduces a contrast after a fact: la utilidad es positiva; sin embargo, el efectivo está comprometido.

examples.es: Estamos cobrando las ventas a treinta días, así que el efectivo llega tarde.
examples.en: We are collecting sales at thirty days, so the cash arrives late.

examples.es: La utilidad es positiva; sin embargo, el efectivo está comprometido.
examples.en: Profit is positive; however, the cash is committed.

lessons.title: Discuss a loan decision with conditions
lessons.objective: Explain in Spanish a loan approval with conditions, separating the approved terms from the items still needing confirmation, using the subjunctive after condición de que and the passive se.
lessons.focus: Subjunctive after condición de que and siempre que for a condition, and se aprobó for an approved decision with pending items.

words.note: An approval that depends on conditions being met.
The amount the lender has agreed to lend.
Requirements that must be met before funds are released.
An asset or person pledged to secure the loan.
The period over which the loan is repaid.
The percentage charged on the loan. Spain usually says tipo de interés; tasa is common in Latin America.
The point at which the money becomes available.
Records still required by the lender.
A mortgage over real estate that secures the loan. In Spain it is signed before a notary.
Insurance covering the pledged asset.
The lender's last written approval before release.
The institution or person providing the loan.
The group that reviews and approves loans.

words.es: El préstamo se aprobó con condiciones.
words.en: The loan was approved with conditions.

words.es: Los fondos se liberan siempre que se firme la garantía.
words.en: The funds are released provided that the security is signed.

words.es: La garantía sigue pendiente de confirmación.
words.en: The guarantee is still pending confirmation.

words.es: ¿Cuál es el monto aprobado y el plazo?
words.en: What is the approved amount and the term?

words.es: Necesitamos la confirmación final por escrito.
words.en: We need the final confirmation in writing.

words.es: No comprometemos ese dinero hasta la liberación.
words.en: We will not commit that money until the release.

lessons.speaking: Walk a small business owner through a conditional loan approval. State the approved amount and term, list two conditions that must be met before funds are released, and identify which items are still being confirmed. Agree the date for the final confirmation.
lessons.partnerRole: Owner who received a conditional loan approval and believes the loan is already fully approved.
lessons.openingLine: El banco aprobó el préstamo. ¿Ya podemos disponer del dinero?

grammar.focus: Con la condición de que and siempre que take the subjunctive for a condition not yet met: los fondos se liberan siempre que se firme la hipoteca. Se aprobó reports the decision without naming who made it. Está pendiente states what is still open.

examples.es: El préstamo se aprobó con la condición de que se firme la garantía hipotecaria.
examples.en: The loan was approved on the condition that the mortgage security is signed.

examples.es: La garantía está pendiente, así que el dinero no se libera todavía.
examples.en: The security is pending, so the money is not released yet.

lessons.title: Negotiate a service scope and fee
lessons.objective: Negotiate a service scope and fee in Spanish for an extra piece of client work, defining the deliverable, exclusions, timing and quoted fee, with a conditional offer.
lessons.focus: Conditional offer (podríamos, incluiríamos), the formal usted with the subjunctive for a client request, and the contrast between incluir and excluir.

words.note: The defined work covered by the fee.
A specific output the client receives.
A piece of work not included in the fee.
The fixed fee for the monthly service.
A report covering three months.
The date by which the deliverable is due.
The fee charged for professional work.
A written price offer. Spain often says presupuesto for a quote.
An adjective: trabajo adicional, cotización adicional.
Confirmation in writing that the scope is accepted.
A change to the agreed work.
Work provided to a client.
A term that must be met.
A check of what is included and excluded.

words.es: Podríamos incluir el informe trimestral si acepta el alcance.
words.en: We could include the quarterly report if you accept the scope.

words.es: El análisis de impuestos está excluido de esta cuota.
words.en: The tax analysis is excluded from this fee.

words.es: Le pedimos que confirme el alcance por escrito.
words.en: We ask you to confirm the scope in writing.

words.es: La cotización adicional llega el viernes.
words.en: The additional quote arrives on Friday.
What would the delivery date be?

words.es: Esta condición cambia los honorarios mensuales.
words.en: This condition changes the monthly fees.

lessons.speaking: Negotiate an extra request from a client who wants a quarterly report added to the monthly service. Define the deliverable and one exclusion, state the timing and the quoted fee, and close by asking the client to confirm the scope in writing.
lessons.partnerRole: Client who wants an additional report and assumes it is included in the current fee.
lessons.openingLine: Quisiera agregar un informe trimestral al servicio mensual. ¿Está incluido en la cuota?

grammar.focus: The conditional makes a formal offer: podríamos incluir el informe si acepta el alcance. Pedir que plus the subjunctive asks the client to act: le pedimos que confirme el alcance. Use excluido for work outside the fee.

examples.es: Podríamos incluir el informe trimestral si confirma el alcance por escrito.
examples.en: We could include the quarterly report if you confirm the scope in writing.

examples.es: El análisis de impuestos está excluido de esta cuota.
examples.en: The tax analysis is excluded from this fee.

lessons.title: Handle an urgent client request during a handoff
lessons.objective: Handle an urgent client request during a handoff in Spanish by explaining what is known, what needs review and when the client will hear back, using the future and the present progressive.
lessons.focus: Future for a firm commitment (le responderemos), the progressive (estamos revisando) for work in progress, and the subjunctive after espero que for a hoped outcome.

words.note: Passing a case or task to a colleague. Entrega de guardia is a shift handover, mostly in healthcare.
A coworker in the same team.
A payment that must be sent quickly.
The current position of a transfer.
Confirmed facts shared with the client.
Open questions not yet answered.
A message sent to keep the client informed.
Proof from the bank that a transfer was processed.
The time when the client will receive an answer.
The task that must come first.
A written summary left for a colleague.
A transaction processed by the bank.
The need for a fast response.
The point at which the transfer arrives at the recipient.

words.es: Lo que sabemos es que el pago salió ayer.
words.en: What we know is that the payment left yesterday.

words.es: Le responderemos antes de las cinco.
words.en: We will respond to you before five o'clock.

words.es: Espero que el banco confirme la operación esta tarde.
words.en: I hope the bank confirms the transaction this afternoon.

words.es: Su colega no está disponible hoy, pero yo sigo el caso.
words.en: Your colleague is not available today, but I am following the case.

words.es: ¿Cuál es el plazo de respuesta que necesita?
words.en: What response time do you need?

lessons.speaking: Take an urgent call from a client whose colleague is unavailable. Say what is known, what is still being reviewed, when the colleague will respond, and what the client should do in the meantime. Close by confirming the time the client will hear back.
lessons.partnerRole: Client who needs a decision today about a bank transfer and is frustrated that the colleague is out.
lessons.openingLine: Necesito una respuesta hoy sobre la transferencia. ¿Dónde está su colega?

grammar.focus: The progressive (estamos revisando) describes work in progress. The future (le responderemos) is a firm commitment. Espero que plus subjunctive states a hoped outcome: espero que el banco confirme hoy. Keep what is known separate from what is still under review.

examples.es: Estamos revisando la transferencia y le responderemos antes de las cinco.
examples.en: We are reviewing the transfer and we will reply before five o'clock.

examples.es: Espero que el banco confirme la operación esta tarde.
examples.en: I hope the bank confirms the transaction this afternoon.

lessons.title: Read a complex reporting note aloud
lessons.objective: Read a complex reporting note aloud in Spanish, turn the technical wording into plain language and check the client's understanding by asking them to explain it back.
lessons.focus: Nominalized technical phrases converted into verb clauses (la variación se debe a... / el resultado refleja...), and the teach-back question ¿Me explica con sus palabras...?

words.note: A plain-language summary of a complex figure.
The difference between two measured amounts.
The final figure after deductions.
An item that does not recur.
Material or service used to produce goods, such as flour for a bakery.
The share of revenue left after direct costs.
An amount set aside for an expected cost.
The act of understanding a financial statement.
The number that matters most in the report.
A version of the note understandable to a non-specialist.
A commitment not yet settled.
The last check before the report is issued.
The meaning drawn from a figure.
The result the note leads to.

words.es: La variación del margen se debe al costo de los insumos.
words.en: The margin variance is due to the cost of supplies.

words.es: ¿Me explica con sus palabras qué significa la nota?
words.en: Could you explain to me in your own words what the note means?
Did you understand the conclusion of the report?

words.es: La provisión es una cantidad apartada para un costo esperado.
words.en: The provision is an amount set aside for an expected cost.

words.es: El resultado neto refleja todas las partidas.
words.en: The net result reflects all the items.

words.es: Lo que queda pendiente es el compromiso del proveedor.
words.en: What remains open is the commitment with the supplier.

lessons.speaking: Read one reporting note aloud to a client, then translate its key technical sentence into plain language. Ask the client to explain back the main conclusion and the open item, correct any misunderstanding, and close with the confirmed meaning.
lessons.partnerRole: Client who receives a technical reporting note and does not understand the wording.
lessons.openingLine: Leí la nota del informe, pero hay palabras que no entiendo. ¿Me la explica?

grammar.focus: Technical nouns can be turned into plain verb clauses: la variación se debe a... (the variance is due to...). Ask for the client's own explanation with ¿Me explica con sus palabras...? and confirm understanding with ¿Entendió usted...?

examples.es: La variación del margen se debe al costo de los insumos.
examples.en: The margin variance is due to the cost of supplies.

examples.es: ¿Me explica con sus palabras qué significa la nota?
examples.en: Could you explain the note to me in your own words?

lessons.title: Discuss an international transfer discrepancy
lessons.objective: Discuss an international transfer discrepancy in Spanish by separating currency conversion, sender fees and possible intermediary fees, without asserting an unknown cause.
lessons.focus: Possible cause with es posible que plus subjunctive, the preterite for the transfer event, and the comparison with según la fuente.

words.note: A payment sent across borders.
A bank that passes funds between the sender's and the recipient's banks.
The fee charged by the sender's bank.
The change of the amount from one currency to another.
The price of one currency in another.
The sum that reaches the recipient.
The sum sent by the client.
A fee for sending money abroad.
The gap between the amount sent and the amount received.
The person or business receiving the payment.
Proof that the transfer was sent.
The date the funds are credited.
The document from which a figure comes.
Transfer option where each side pays its own bank; fees from other banks may reduce the amount received.

words.es: Es posible que un banco intermediario haya cobrado una comisión.
words.en: It is possible that an intermediary bank charged a fee.

words.es: Según el extracto del banco, se cobró una comisión de remesa.
words.en: According to the bank statement, a remittance fee was charged.

words.es: El importe recibido es menor que el importe enviado.
words.en: The amount received is less than the amount sent.

words.es: ¿Qué fuente de datos muestra el tipo de cambio aplicado?
words.en: Which data source shows the exchange rate applied?

words.es: Envió el pago el lunes desde su cuenta.
words.en: You sent the payment on Monday from your account.

words.es: Necesitamos el justificante de envío para confirmar la diferencia.
words.en: We need the transfer confirmation to confirm the difference.

lessons.speaking: Explain to a client why the recipient received less than the sender transferred. Separate the currency conversion, the sender fee and any possible intermediary fee, state which part is known, and agree the source document you need to confirm the rest.
lessons.partnerRole: Client who sent 2,000 euros to a foreign supplier and was told the supplier received less.
lessons.openingLine: Mandé 2.000 euros al proveedor del extranjero y recibió menos. ¿Qué pasó con la diferencia?

grammar.focus: Es posible que plus the subjunctive names a possible cause without asserting it: es posible que un banco intermediario haya cobrado una comisión. Según plus a source attributes a figure: según el extracto, se cobró una comisión. The preterite reports the completed transfer.

examples.es: Es posible que un banco intermediario haya cobrado una comisión.
examples.en: It is possible that an intermediary bank charged a fee.

examples.es: Según el extracto del banco, se cobró una comisión de remesa.
examples.en: According to the bank statement, a remittance fee was charged.

lessons.title: Explain a compliance information request
lessons.objective: Explain an additional compliance information request from a bank in Spanish, state why it was made and name the approved submission route, using the passive with ser and formal imperatives.
lessons.focus: Passive with ser plus participle (la solicitud fue enviada), impersonal se for the approved route, and formal imperatives for guidance to the client.

words.note: A formal request for records or explanations.
Meeting the rules and deadlines set by the authority.
The channel the authority accepts for submissions.
The online system for sending documents.
A receipt confirming a submission was received.
Where money came from; banks ask for evidence of it in compliance reviews.
Records requested beyond the usual set.
The stated purpose of the request.
A formal demand to provide information or documents.
The last date for sending the records.
The checks a bank must carry out on its customers and their transactions.
A copy confirmed as true to the original.

words.es: La solicitud fue emitida por el banco.
words.en: The request was issued by the bank.

words.es: Envíe los documentos por el portal oficial.
words.en: Send the documents through the official portal.

words.es: Se envía con el acuse de recibo.
words.en: It is sent with the acknowledgment of receipt.

words.es: ¿Cuál es el motivo de la solicitud?
words.en: What is the reason for the request?

words.es: No podemos enviarlo por un canal no autorizado.
words.en: We cannot send it through an unauthorized channel.

words.es: Guarde el acuse en el expediente.
words.en: Keep the acknowledgment in the file.

lessons.speaking: Respond to a client who questions an extra document request from the bank's compliance team. Explain what the request asks for, why it was issued in general terms, and the approved route for submitting. Close by confirming the route and the date the client will submit.
lessons.partnerRole: Client who thinks the request is excessive and wants to send the documents by an informal route.
lessons.openingLine: Me llegó otra solicitud de documentos, y no entiendo por qué la piden otra vez.

grammar.focus: The passive with ser plus participle states a completed request: la solicitud fue emitida por la autoridad. Passive se states the route without naming the agent: la solicitud se envía por el portal oficial; las solicitudes se envían por el portal oficial. Formal imperatives give guidance: envíe los documentos por el portal, y guarde el acuse.

examples.es: La solicitud fue emitida por el banco para verificar el origen de los fondos.
examples.en: The request was issued by the bank to verify the source of the funds.

examples.es: Envíe los documentos por el portal oficial y guarde el acuse.
examples.en: Send the documents through the official portal and keep the acknowledgment.

lessons.title: Respond to pressure to change a record
lessons.objective: Respond to pressure from a client to record an unsupported entry in Spanish by explaining the missing evidence and proposing a documented next step, using negative imperatives and the conditional to make an offer.
lessons.focus: Negative formal imperatives (no registre, no incluya) for refusal, the conditional (podríamos, documentaríamos) for an offer, and the subjunctive after no creo que for a doubtful claim.

words.note: The evidence that proves a transaction.
An expense with no evidence on file.
An entry that does not follow the rules or the evidence.
An item held open until evidence arrives.
Written proof for a transaction.
The account where expenses are recorded.
Demand to change a record in a particular way.
A change made to a record after review.
A note in the file explaining a decision.
The duty to keep records accurate.
The date by which the evidence must arrive.
An amount subtracted before tax, where the rules of the jurisdiction allow it and evidence supports it.
The end of an accounting period.

words.es: No registre el pago como gasto sin el justificante.
words.en: Do not record the payment as an expense without the supporting document.
We could record it as a pending item.

words.es: No creo que podamos clasificarlo sin prueba.
words.en: I do not think we can classify it without evidence.

words.es: Guardamos una nota interna con la decisión.
words.en: We keep an internal note with the decision.
When could you send us the documentary evidence?

words.es: Entiendo la urgencia, pero no podemos cambiar el registro.
words.en: I understand the urgency, but we cannot change the record.

lessons.speaking: Respond to a client who asks you to record a payment that has no supporting document. Refuse to record it without evidence, explain what evidence is missing, and propose a documented next step. Close by agreeing the date for the evidence.
lessons.partnerRole: Client who wants a payment recorded as an expense without any receipt, because the amount is important to him.
lessons.openingLine: Quiero que registre este pago como gasto aunque no tengamos el recibo. Es urgente.

grammar.focus: Negative usted commands give a clear instruction: no registre el pago como gasto. The conditional offers a documented option: podríamos registrarlo como partida pendiente. No creo que plus the subjunctive questions a claim: no creo que podamos clasificarlo sin prueba.

examples.es: No registre el pago como gasto sin el justificante correspondiente.
examples.en: Do not record the payment as an expense without the corresponding supporting document.

examples.es: Podríamos registrarlo como partida pendiente si nos envía la prueba.
examples.en: We could record it as a pending item if you send us the evidence.

lessons.title: Prepare a management briefing
lessons.objective: Prepare a short management briefing in Spanish that prioritizes cash, reporting and deadline questions for a fictional business, using a numbered list read aloud and the future for decisions to be taken.
lessons.focus: Future for decisions still to be taken (tomaremos), the ordering phrases en primer lugar and por último, and the priority vocabulary.

words.note: The item that must be handled first.
Cash in and out over a period.
The report of results for the month.
The last date for an action.
A choice that must be made.
A formal meeting of managers or owners.
The person who owns the decision.
A payment not yet made.
Cash held back for needs.
A possible unfavorable outcome.
A short summary for the decision maker.
The schedule of dates for payments.
The last date for action.
A step taken to fix a problem.

words.es: En primer lugar, tomaremos la decisión sobre el efectivo.
words.en: First, we will take the decision about the cash.

words.es: En segundo lugar, revisaremos el informe mensual.
words.en: Second, we will review the monthly report.

words.es: Por último, confirmemos la fecha límite de entrega.
words.en: Finally, let's confirm the delivery deadline.

words.es: ¿Quién es el responsable de cada decisión?
words.en: Who is responsible for each decision?

words.es: Hay un riesgo de liquidez si pagamos todo esta semana.
words.en: There is a liquidity risk if we pay everything this week.

words.es: Esta prioridad necesita una acción correctiva.
words.en: This priority needs a corrective action.

lessons.speaking: Give a five-minute management briefing for a fictional business. Prioritize three items (cash, reporting and deadline), state the decision each one needs, and say who owns each decision. Close by asking the manager to confirm the order of priorities.
lessons.partnerRole: Manager who has only a few minutes and wants the three most urgent items in order.
lessons.openingLine: Tengo diez minutos antes de la junta. ¿Cuáles son las prioridades de la empresa?

grammar.focus: The future states a decision still to be taken: tomaremos la decisión el viernes. Ordering phrases introduce priorities: en primer lugar, en segundo lugar, por último. Use the infinitive after the noun for the task: la decisión de pagar primero al proveedor.

examples.es: En primer lugar, tomaremos la decisión sobre el efectivo esta semana.
examples.en: First, we will make the decision about cash this week.

examples.es: Por último, debemos confirmar la fecha límite de entrega al banco.
examples.en: Finally, we must confirm the deadline for delivery to the bank.

lessons.title: Teach a new coworker a review process
lessons.objective: Teach a new coworker a review process in Spanish by explaining the sequence, asking for a teach-back and correcting an overlooked check respectfully, using the imperative for the sequence and the subjunctive for a request.
lessons.focus: Sequence words (primero, luego, después, al final), tú commands for a peer, and te pido que plus the subjunctive for a respectful correction.

words.note: The sequence of checks for a payment file.
A list of checks to complete in order.
The authorization to proceed.
The code that links a payment to a document.
The money figure on the document.
The evidence for a transaction.
The set of records for one payment: invoice, support and approval.
A review step that was not completed.
A fix made to a record.
The act of acquiring a skill or practice.
The person who signs off a step.
The last check before the file is closed.
The order of steps in a process.
Information given to improve a result.

words.es: Primero revisa la factura, luego compara el importe.
words.en: First check the invoice, then compare the amount.

words.es: Te pido que revises la referencia antes de aprobar.
words.en: I ask you to check the reference before approving.
Can you repeat it back to me in your own words?
words.note: Tú form for a colleague. With a client: ¿Me lo repite con sus palabras?

words.es: Revisamos el archivo de pago paso a paso.
words.en: We review the payment file step by step.

words.es: Falta un control en la lista de verificación.
words.en: One check is missing from the checklist.

words.es: Vamos a corregirlo juntos antes del cierre.
words.en: We are going to correct it together before the close.

lessons.speaking: Teach a new coworker the review steps for a payment file. Explain the sequence, ask the coworker to repeat the steps back to you, and correct one check that was skipped without blaming the coworker. Close by agreeing the revised sequence.
lessons.partnerRole: New coworker who is learning the review process and is eager but worried about making a mistake.
lessons.openingLine: Quiero aprender bien el proceso de revisión. ¿Por dónde empiezo?

grammar.focus: Sequence words organize steps: primero, luego, después, al final. Use tú commands with a peer: revisa primero la factura. Te pido que plus the subjunctive corrects respectfully: te pido que revises la referencia. Ask for a teach-back: ¿Me lo repites con tus palabras?

examples.es: Primero revisa la factura, luego compara el importe con el justificante.
examples.en: First check the invoice, then compare the amount with the supporting document.

examples.es: Te pido que revises la referencia antes de aprobar el pago.
examples.en: I ask you to check the reference before approving the payment.

lessons.title: Complete a complex professional case
lessons.objective: Complete a complex professional case in Spanish: reconcile conflicting records, discuss a changed estimate and close with a precise handoff to the client and the team.
lessons.focus: Combined tenses for an integrated case: preterite and present perfect for events and progress, the subjunctive for doubt and request, the conditional for an offer, and the future for the next commitment.

words.note: Two records that disagree on the same item.
A changed estimate after new information.
The matching of records.
An item still unresolved.
The first record used to verify a figure.
Passing the case to a colleague.
A summary given at the close of a case.
A list of what will be done and by whom.
The person who owns each step.
The person or business the case serves.
The current position of the case.
The effect of a change on the tax position, where applicable.
Written proof a decision was agreed.
The last promised action with a date.

words.es: El cobro llegó en mayo y hemos conciliado casi todo.
words.en: The payment came in in May, and we have reconciled almost everything.

words.es: No creo que el segundo registro sea correcto.
words.en: I do not think the second record is correct.

words.es: Le pedimos que envíe la fuente original.
words.en: We ask you to send the original source.

words.es: Podríamos actualizar la estimación con esa fuente.
words.en: We could update the estimate with that source.

words.es: Traspasaremos el caso a Mauro mañana.
words.en: We will hand the case over to Mauro tomorrow.

words.es: El estado del caso queda claro por escrito.
words.en: The case status is clear in writing.

lessons.speaking: Lead a final case discussion with the client and a teammate. Summarize the conflicting records, the changed estimate and the open item. State what the team has completed, what is still uncertain, and the handoff to the colleague. Close by repeating the final action and its date to the client.
lessons.partnerRole: Self-employed client in Spain who needs a precise close, with a clear list of what changed and what is still open; a teammate joins the call.
lessons.openingLine: Tenemos dos registros que no coinciden y una estimación que cambió. ¿Cómo lo cerramos hoy?

grammar.focus: Combine the tenses already studied: the preterite for events (llegó, cambió), the present perfect for progress (hemos conciliado), the subjunctive for doubt and request (no creo que, le pedimos que), the conditional for an offer (podríamos), and the future for the next commitment (traspasaremos). Close with a clear next action and a date.

examples.es: El cobro llegó en mayo y hemos conciliado casi todos los registros.
examples.en: The payment came in in May, and we have reconciled almost all the records.

examples.es: No creo que el segundo registro sea correcto; le pedimos que envíe la fuente.
examples.en: I do not think the second record is correct; we ask you to send the source.
